stem: Mile High Robotics is standardizing how its platform team provisions cloud servers across three regional offices. They want the exact target setup captured somewhere any engineer can read, diff, and re-run instead of re-deriving it from memory. Which practice satisfies this?

choices.text: Keep the desired resource configuration in a versioned file that states the end result, and apply it through the same process every time.
Configure each new office's servers directly through the cloud console, matching the previous office's settings from memory each time.
Write a script that issues a fixed sequence of cloud CLI commands whenever a new office's servers are needed.
Bake a golden server image with the desired setup once, and redeploy new instances from that image at each office.

rationale: The key states the desired end result in a versioned file and reapplies it through one consistent process, which is exactly what Infrastructure as Code is. Configuring each office through the console from memory has nothing written down to read or diff at all. An ordered CLI script encodes steps rather than an end state, so it cannot be diffed against what already exists the way a declarative file can. A golden image bakes the setup into an opaque artifact; an engineer cannot read or diff the individual settings inside it the way they can a configuration file.
